items.title: Kimberly Clark (KMB) Launches Desert Plant Toilet Paper Program
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark has launched a proprietary program to develop toilet paper using fibers from a drought-resistant desert plant called hesperaloe. The initiative is supported by internal testing and a pilot facility in Arizona that focuses on scaling hesperaloe-based hygiene materials. The program aims to reduce reliance on traditional wood-based fibers and address environmental and supply chain concerns in tissue production. items.title: A ‘Goldilocks’ Discovery in the Paper Aisle
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark  the maker of Scott paper towels and Cottonelle toilet paper, is exploring an alternative to making its products from trees, Natasha Khan reports.  It says a prickly desert plant called hesperaloe produces fiber that can make stronger and softer paper products.  Kimberly-Clark cautions that there is a long research runway ahead, but a viable tree alternative would be a scientific breakthrough capable of reshaping the consumer-products landscape.
